questions.q: How do this lesson's DMVs differ from Chapter 7's DMV coverage?
options: Chapter 7's DMVs cover general instance health (sessions, CPU, memory, I/O); this lesson's DMVs are specific to query performance -- which cached queries are consuming the most resources
They are exactly the same DMVs, just renamed
This lesson's DMVs only work on Azure SQL Managed Instance
Chapter 7 already covered sys.dm_exec_query_stats in full, so this lesson repeats it
questions.explain: This lesson narrows in on the plan cache and per-query cumulative statistics specifically.

questions.q: How does sys.dm_exec_query_stats differ from Query Store as a source of 'worst queries' information?
options: It reads live from the current plan cache with no setup required, but nothing persists once a plan is evicted or the instance restarts -- unlike Query Store's persisted history
They are functionally identical in every way
sys.dm_exec_query_stats requires ALTER DATABASE to enable, just like Query Store
Query Store cannot show cumulative statistics, only sys.dm_exec_query_stats can
questions.explain: Use the DMVs for 'what's expensive right now,' and Query Store for 'was this always slow, with history over time.'

options: Converts an opaque sql_handle from sys.dm_exec_query_stats into readable query text
Deletes a query's cached plan
Forces a query to recompile immediately
Shows only queries written by sysadmin logins
questions.explain: sys.dm_exec_query_stats returns sql_handle and plan_handle as opaque identifiers, not the actual query text or plan.

questions.q: Why is CROSS APPLY the right join type to pair sys.dm_exec_query_stats with sys.dm_exec_sql_text?
options: CROSS APPLY calls the table-valued function once per row of the outer query, passing that row's own sql_handle in -- exactly the row-by-row pattern needed here
CROSS APPLY is required because sys.dm_exec_sql_text has no parameters
CROSS APPLY prevents the query from ever returning more than one row
CROSS APPLY only works with sys.dm_exec_query_plan, never sys.dm_exec_sql_text
questions.explain: This is the same CROSS APPLY pattern from T-SQL Development, applied to a DMV-based function call per row.

questions.q: What can you do with the result of sys.dm_exec_query_plan(qs.plan_handle)?
options: Click the returned XML in SSMS results and it renders as the same graphical execution plan covered in Lesson 45, without re-running the query
It can only be viewed as raw, unformatted text with no graphical rendering possible
It automatically forces that plan for future executions
It only works for queries that have never actually executed
questions.explain: This is useful for seeing the exact plan that already ran for a query you may not be able to re-run yourself.
